messages:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a regression after the kernel-selector tweak. Mistral-int8 p95 latency +~20-25% on short-chat workload, and a small quality slip on our calibration evals. Repro steps below.

Alex: ```
run_profile --model mistral-7b --quant int8 --batch 1 --seq 64 --traces
```

Priya: I reproduced. Looks related to the calibration change in PR#872 (we switched to moment-based per-tensor stats, down from per-layer histograms). Microbench attached.

Priya: ```
KernelSelector v2 -> v3
mistral-7b/int8:
p50: 45ms -> 56ms (+24%)
p95: 90ms -> 108ms (+20%)
tokens/sec: 220 -> 178
kv_copy time: 3% -> 12%
```

Sam: Confirmed the kv_copy spike. When prefix > 32 tokens we see frequent KV evictions and memcpy churn. Trace shows hot path in kv_copy and memcpy.

Nina: Uploaded flamegraph: /artifacts/1963123456-mistral-int8-flame.svg :eyes: Also eval diffs: our dialed-in prompt set shows a 0.6% delta on quality metric.

Alex: Priya — did the calib mode change per-layer -> global? That could explain layer-level dynamic range mismatches.

Priya: Yes. We moved from per-layer 256-bin histogram -> per-tensor moment estimate to speed up calib. It underestimates outliers on some Mistral layers, which pushes the kernel selector to pick JJIT mixed-fp8 fallback on a subset of layers, increasing compute and causing KV churn. Reverting gives quality and latency back but costs more sampling time.

Diego: Did a quick experiment with calib_samples=5000. Results look better:

Diego: ```
calib_samples=5000
model=mistral-7b
quant=int8
run_perf --calib $calib_samples
=> p50 48ms, p95 92ms, tokens/sec 205
quality delta: -0.1%
```

Sam: Proposed mitigations: 1) adaptive fallback — keep per-layer hist when activation variance > threshold, 2) prefer int8 kernels for layers with high dynamic range, 3) batching heuristic: pin short-prefix low-batch requests to hot workers to avoid KV eviction for those flows.

Priya: +1 on adaptive per-layer. Also we should add a CI perf/regression test that runs the short-chat profile on Mistral-int8 and enforces p95 and quality bounds.

Alex: I'll open an RFC and a hotfix PR to revert the calibration change while we design the adaptive approach. Assigning owners: Alex (hotfix), Priya (calib logic), Sam (kv pinning), Diego (bench infra).

perf-bot: Scheduled perf job 1963123500 completed. Artifacts uploaded to the run: ci://perf/1963123500.

Nina: One more ask — can we snapshot equivalent runs for Qwen and Llama configs to see cross-model sensitivity? Mistral seems particularly sensitive to per-layer extremas.

Alex: Good call. We'll share a common bucket for quant-profiles and a short README for when to prefer per-layer vs per-tensor. Pinging @eng-runtime and @eng-ml for visibility.

Priya: For the hotfix I'll revert the moment-based path and add a flag so we can A/B the new logic behind an opt-in.

Sam: I'll prototype KV pinning in the routing policy; small-batch sticky assignment should be cheap and might eliminate the memcpy spike.

Diego: I'll add the short-chat benchmark to perf CI and a quality check against the calibration eval set.

Alex: Thanks everyone. Summary: hotfix first, then design adaptive per-layer heuristics and routing pin. Track in the RFC and tag the perf artifacts. :thumbsup:
